page: Microsoft Azure F2ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, backed by 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the F2ams_v6 demonstrates strong single-core compute capabilities, as evidenced by its top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing also rank in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads show distinct performance limitations. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the lower 25 percent, reflecting the physical constraints of a 2-core configuration. Memory bandwidth benchmarks present a mixed profile, with write operations scoring in the average range while read-only bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks register in the bottom 25 percent. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput are also weak, positioning this instance away from high-throughput transactional roles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F2ams_v6 offers a highly specialized resource profile, delivering a generous 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without the overhead of high core counts. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. It is well-suited for light memory-intensive tasks, single-threaded data processing, small-scale text processing, and basic LLM inference using small models, where prompt processing and text generation perform at average speeds. Conversely, it is less suitable for multi-threaded compilation, heavy database hosting, or high-concurrency web serving due to its lower multi-core efficiency and restricted memory read bandwidth.

Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 2 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio.
